hook: *Daddy Yankee* is Person of the Year. Clear your *Thursday*.
dek: The Latin Grammys are Thursday, November 12, in Las Vegas. A Willie Colón tribute, a stacked stage and the races to watch.

slides.label: When and where
slides.text: *Thursday, November 12*, MGM Grand Garden Arena, Las Vegas. On *Univision*, hosted by *Roselyn Sánchez*.

slides.label: The headline
slides.text: *Daddy Yankee* is the Latin Recording Academy's *Person of the Year*, and he performs. Reggaeton went from mixtapes to *the Academy's highest honor*.

slides.label: Bronx roots
slides.text: The show plans a tribute to *Willie Colón*, who helped build the *New York salsa sound* out of the South Bronx.

slides.label: Just added
slides.text: *Karol G, Bizarrap and Bad Gyal* join a stage with *Rosalía, Anitta, Feid, Carín León, Grupo Frontera, Juanes* and more.

slides.label: Races to watch
slides.text: *Karol G*, *CA7RIEL & Paco Amoroso* and *Rosalía* are among the top nominees. Rosalía is up for *Album and Record of the Year*.

slides.label: The Den's take
slides.text: Reggaeton, regional Mexican, flamenco pop, Argentine rap and a salsa legend's legacy *on one stage*. Latin music is *every sound*.

caption_instagram:
Latin Grammys 2026: Thursday, November 12, at the MGM Grand Garden Arena in Las Vegas, on Univision with host Roselyn Sánchez. 🎤

Daddy Yankee is the Latin Recording Academy's Person of the Year and will perform. Reggaeton went from mixtapes and car speakers to the Academy's highest honor.

The show also plans a tribute to Willie Colón, who helped build the New York salsa sound out of the South Bronx. Just added to the lineup: Karol G, Bizarrap and Bad Gyal, joining Rosalía, Anitta, Feid, Carín León, Grupo Frontera, Juanes and more.

caption_linkedin:
Few industries show the power of culture-led growth like Latin music.

At the Latin Grammys on November 12, the Latin Recording Academy honors Daddy Yankee as Person of the Year, a genre that grew from Puerto Rico's mixtapes into a global business. The same night pays tribute to Willie Colón, whose work helped build New York salsa, and puts reggaeton, regional Mexican, flamenco pop and Argentine rap on one stage.

The lesson for builders: audiences that were overlooked by the industry often become its fastest-growing markets.

Which underestimated audience is your industry still overlooking?

By The Innovators Den.
